title: Scorpio cabbage (Scorpio F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Scorpio cabbage is an F1 hybrid cabbage variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Scorpio cabbage is an F1 hybrid cabbage variety, also sold or known as Scorpio F1 or Scorpio repolyo. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Sakata (sold by Allied Botanical).

heroImage.alt: Vegetable terraces and plastic tunnels on the slopes of Mankayan, Benguet, the kind of farm where Scorpio cabbage is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Scorpio F1 or Scorpio repolyo, this is the same cabbage. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [cabbage variety finder](/crop-varieties/cabbage), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit cabbage fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [black rot of cabbage](/diseases/black-rot), [cabbage webworm](/pests/cabbage-webworm), [clubroot](/diseases/clubroot), [diamondback moth](/pests/diamondback-moth). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** 55 to 60 days in the guide, Allied gives 65 to 70 days after transplanting.
**Yield:** About 21 t/ha marketable, averaged over three Benguet sites and four seasons under organic growing (BSU trial).
**Fruit:** Head: round, compact, small core, purple veins, about 1 to 1.2 kg (Allied).
Highest heading percentage across sites in the trial.
Heat tolerant and juicy with a slight sweetness (Allied claim).

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: check variety in a cabbage trial, which calls it the variety Benguet farmers had commonly planted for more than 10 years, also listed in the cabbage production guide. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual cabbage on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Scorpio cabbage

Most repolyo comes from the highlands, where it heads well. Lowland growers need a heat tolerant hybrid and a cool month. Pick a firm head that keeps on the trip to market. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

items.q: Is Scorpio F1 the same as Scorpio?
items.a: Yes. Scorpio F1 is another name for Scorpio. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Scorpio?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
